definitions.explanation: Of outstanding importance, achievement, or ability.
The quality of being great or distinguished.

examples.japanese: {偉大|いだい}⟦な→な：09497_na⟧⟦{科学者|かがくしゃ}→科学者：19378_kagakusha⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
{偉大|いだい}⟦な→な：09497_na⟧⟦{業績|ぎょうせき}→業績：04873_gyouseki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{残|のこ}した→残す：01975_nokosu⟧。
⟦{歴史|れきし}→歴史：02267_rekishi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{残|のこ}る→残る：01187_nokoru⟧{偉大|いだい}⟦な→な：09497_na⟧⟦{発明|はつめい}→発明：01495_hatsumei⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: It is a great invention that will go down in history.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{偉大|いだい}さ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{感|かん}じた→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧。
⟦{自然|しぜん}→自然：01423_shizen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{偉大|いだい}さ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{圧倒|あっとう}された→圧倒：12044_attou⟧。
examples.english: I was overwhelmed by the greatness of nature.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{作品|さくひん}→作品：02776_sakuhin⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}る→見る：00283_miru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦{芸術家|げいじゅつか}→芸術家：14979_geijutsuka⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{偉大|いだい}さ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{分|わ}かる→分かる：00463_wakaru⟧。
examples.english: Looking at this work, you can really appreciate the artist's greatness.

notes:
{偉大|いだい} describes outstanding greatness in achievement, character, or scale. Used for historical figures, remarkable accomplishments, and the grandeur of nature.

FORMS:
- Na-adjective: {偉大|いだい}⟦な→な：09497_na⟧⟦{発明|はつめい}→発明：01495_hatsumei⟧ (a great invention)
- Noun: {偉大|いだい}さ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{感|かん}じる→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧ (to feel the greatness)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {偉大|いだい}⟦な→な：09497_na⟧⟦{人物|じんぶつ}→人物：03356_jinbutsu⟧: great person/figure
- {偉大|いだい}⟦な→な：09497_na⟧⟦{功績|こうせき}→功績：04143_kouseki⟧ / ⟦{業績|ぎょうせき}→業績：04873_gyouseki⟧: great achievement
- {偉大|いだい}⟦な→な：09497_na⟧⟦{指導者|しどうしゃ}→指導者：03062_shidousha⟧: great leader
- {偉大|いだい}⟦な→な：09497_na⟧⟦{自然|しぜん}→自然：01423_shizen⟧: the grandeur of nature

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{偉|えら}い→偉い：00039_erai⟧: great, admirable (casual, also means "of high rank")
- {偉大|いだい}: great, magnificent (formal, literary)
- ⟦{立派|りっぱ}→立派：01093_rippa⟧: splendid, admirable (more everyday)

REGISTER:
Formal and somewhat literary. Used in speeches, written text, and when discussing achievements with gravity.
